newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New U.N. chief calls in resignations from top staff.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. chief calls in resignations from top staff.

text.p: Kofi Annan, the incoming U.N. secretary-general, has asked for the resignations of about two dozen senior staff, U.N. officials said on Monday.
The letters, they said, were sent out on Friday and were not tantamount to firing. But they would allow Annan to decide which staff members to keep or replace.
Annan, 58, undersecretary-general for peacekeeping, takes over the top U.N. post from Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Jan. 1.

It was the first time blanket requests for resignations were done in writing shortly before the Christmas and New Year holidays. In the past, individuals either resigned or were asked quietly to do so when a new secretary-general's term began.
The letter went to about 23 undersecretaries-general and assistant secretaries general.
Excluded were those involved in peacekeeping and peacemaking as well as special representatives in various field locations. This was done for the sake of continuity, the officials said.

Excluded also were those undersecretaries-general whose appointments were approved by the General Assembly or in consultation with other bodies, such as the executive board of the U.N. Children's Fund or the World Food Programme. Both are headed by Americans.
